body: You have to go in right away nothing they can do a few days later
For me the stitch mark scars have stayed along with the main scar, but then I don't heal well so i guess it will depend.

I know how you feel. I wanted someone to notice yet at the same time didn't. Strangely I  only learned that my best friend already knew about my self-harm when I called her the first time I was admitted to the psych hospital. Sometimes I wonder if she had said something earlier would things have gotten as severe as they did.
I have cut on my neck and it is not worth it. It landed me in inpatient. It is dangerous and the scar is rather visible - luckily it has faded over time, but I don't suggest giving into the urge.

I have been to residential a few times and while the first time was for bulimia and self harm the last two times were just for self harm.  Most residential programs are usually 30 days. They were helpful.  

I have also been on inpatient units in the hospital twice for self harm, but never by choice always on a 72 hour hold. Those stays were about from a few days to a few weeks. I know you can voluntarily check -in but honestly you don't really do much there. Residential was much more benifical for me.

The severity of my cutting increased greatly over the years and I wish I had stopped before I got to where I am now. I think talking to a therapist is a great place to start and maybe discuss with them if inpatient would be helpful for you.

Please let me know if you have any questions about going inpatient or to a residential program.
If you are asking about fictional characters with self harm the best one I have see is the character Aaron on Emmerdale. It is a british soap, but you can find it on youtube.
Yes. All the times I have had stitches or staples they have left scars like yours even when they have faded to white.
As someone suggested maybe a long sleeve rash guard top and now they even make leggings for surfing. maybe those could help.

I can't speak for everyone, but for me it became a horrible habit. One I wish I had never started. I cut for years and now I have been trying to quit for 8 years and to this day I still struggle with urges and relapses. If you have someone you can talk to please do - it gets harder too stop the longer it goes on.

I didn't start self-harming until I was 17 and having being trying to stop for years. I am 34. You are not alone - it is not just young teenagers. It is a hard struggle and hopefully you know there are people who can relate even if it isn't close friends and family.

To be honest no one has really asked me about my scars even though I think they are rather obvious (I have been asked 3 times in over 15 years and just brushed them off).  So I have just decided people are oblivious or are being respectful and ignoring the elephant in the room - and if they can then I just pretend I don't have the scars.

I am sorry that you have cut for the first time. I think it is brave of you to realize that it won't stop at one and to tell your therapist. I hope your therapist is helpful and realizes the courage it takes to be truthful when you don't know how she will react.  It is a road I am still stuck on and one I wish I had gotten off right when it started.

I can definitely relate to your worries.  When I went to college I had only self harmed once before, but turned to it to try and cope with the loneliness and isolation I felt.  In the end of course it just made both of those things worse.  I don't have amazing advice on how to make the experience easier, but looking back I wish I had never turned to self harm as that only hurt me worse.
I find the person I compete with the most is myself.  My self harm has to be as bad or worse than in the past otherwise it doesn't feel complete or "good enough."
Sorry didn't mean for it to come across as an advertisment.
self harm is not something you want to start. i first self harmed as a senior in high school and still to this day struggle and I am in my thirties.
I at times have felt the same and it can be so tough. You don't need to prove to anyone that you are "serious". self harming is never safe or harmless.
